title: Varicose veins + stasis dermatitis: incompetent venous valves
vignette: A 54-year-old woman comes to the office due to aching and heaviness in her legs that worsens after prolonged standing and improves with leg elevation. She has had several pregnancies and works long shifts on her feet. Examination shows dilated, tortuous superficial veins along the medial aspect of both lower legs, with brownish hyperpigmentation and dry, scaly skin over the medial ankles. A photograph of the affected leg is shown. Incompetence of which of the following structures is most likely responsible for this patient's findings?

clues.text: worsens after prolonged standing and improves with leg elevation
clues.note: Symptoms driven by gravity (worse with standing, better with elevation) indicate a venous, pressure-dependent process - chronic venous insufficiency.
Dilated tortuous superficial veins are varicose veins, the visible result of sustained venous hypertension from failed valves.

clues.text: brownish hyperpigmentation and dry, scaly skin over the medial ankles
clues.note: Hemosiderin-driven brown hyperpigmentation and stasis dermatitis at the medial ankle are hallmarks of chronic venous insufficiency.

whatMatters: Leg heaviness worse with standing/better with elevation + varicose veins + medial-ankle hyperpigmentation and stasis dermatitis = chronic venous insufficiency. The primary defect is incompetent VENOUS VALVES: when valves fail, blood refluxes and pools, raising venous pressure and producing varicosities and skin changes. Answer F.
strategy: Recognize chronic venous insufficiency, then name the failing structure: one-way venous valves normally prevent backflow against gravity. Their incompetence -> venous hypertension -> varicosities + stasis skin changes. Reject arterial, lymphatic, and capillary structures - the gravity-dependent, elevation-relieved pattern is venous.

eliminations.label: Arterial elastic lamina - arterial, not venous
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the elastic layers of arterial walls. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: arterial disease causes claudication and diminished pulses, not varicosities or elevation-relieved heaviness. ✅ Correct if: peripheral arterial disease / aneurysm.

eliminations.label: Capillary basement membrane - not the primary defect
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the basement membrane of capillaries (thickened in diabetic microangiopathy). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't produce varicose veins or valvular reflux. ✅ Correct if: diabetic microvascular disease.

eliminations.label: Deep venous thrombus - acute, different picture
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an acute clot occluding a deep vein. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: DVT presents acutely with unilateral swelling/pain; this is a chronic, bilateral picture with varicosities (though prior DVT can secondarily damage valves). ✅ Correct if: acute unilateral leg swelling and pain.

eliminations.label: Lymphatic channels - causes lymphedema, not varicosities
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: lymphatic vessels; their failure causes lymphedema. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: lymphedema is non-pitting swelling (often dorsum of foot, positive Stemmer sign) without varicose veins or hemosiderin staining. ✅ Correct if: lymphedema after node dissection/filariasis.

eliminations.label: Precapillary sphincters - regulate flow, not valves
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: smooth-muscle sphincters that regulate capillary perfusion. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they control microcirculatory flow, not venous return; their function is unrelated to varicose veins. ✅ Correct if: local capillary blood-flow regulation.

reasoning: Leg heaviness worse standing/better elevated + varicose veins + medial-ankle stasis skin changes = chronic venous insufficiency
Normal venous return depends on one-way valves preventing gravitational backflow
Incompetent valves -> reflux, venous pooling, and venous hypertension -> varicosities + skin changes
mechanism: Venous return from the legs works against gravity and depends on the calf muscle pump plus one-way venous valves that prevent retrograde flow. When these valves become incompetent (from prolonged standing, pregnancy, obesity, or prior deep venous thrombosis), blood refluxes and pools in the superficial system, chronically elevating venous pressure. Sustained venous hypertension dilates and elongates superficial veins into varicose veins and forces fluid, proteins, and red cells into the interstitium. Extravasated red cells break down, depositing hemosiderin that produces the characteristic brown medial-ankle hyperpigmentation and stasis dermatitis; advanced disease leads to venous stasis ulcers over the medial malleolus. Management is leg elevation and graduated compression stockings. Arterial, lymphatic, and capillary structures do not produce this valve-failure pattern.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid CV > chronic venous insufficiency: incompetent venous valves -> venous hypertension -> varicose veins, medial-ankle stasis dermatitis/hyperpigmentation, venous ulcers; risk factors standing/pregnancy/obesity/prior DVT.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: The gravity-dependent, elevation-relieved symptoms plus varicosities and hemosiderin staining localize the defect to venous valves.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on venous valve, chronic venous insufficiency, stasis dermatitis, hemosiderin, or calf muscle pump? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Arterial (claudication), lymphatic (lymphedema, no varicosities), capillary BM (diabetic micro), precapillary sphincters (flow control) don't fit.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.message: On the leg photo: dilated tortuous superficial veins with brown discoloration and scaling at the medial ankle. Anchor: 'varicose veins + brown medial-ankle skin = incompetent venous valves.'

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: chronic venous insufficiency = valve incompetence -> venous hypertension; treat with compression + elevation.

memoryHook: Failed venous valves let blood fall back down the leg - it pools, veins bulge, and iron-stained skin browns at the ankle.
